info.title: Merge sort is old
info.text: John von Neumann described the merge sort in 1945, on one of the first stored-program computers.

info.title: Recursion
info.text: Merge sort naturally calls itself on each half, which is called recursion. You meet it properly at A level.

info.title: Real sorts are hybrids
info.text: The sort built into most programming languages switches to insertion sort for small pieces, because it is faster there.

info.title: Cards in your hand
info.text: Almost everyone sorts a hand of cards with an insertion sort without being taught it.

info.title: Stable sorts
info.text: Merge and insertion sorts keep equal items in their original order, which matters when sorting records by more than one field.

info.title: Exam tip
info.text: Show the list after each pass, clearly labelled. Marks are given for the intermediate states, not just the final answer.
